title.en: Biographies of Zhang Er and Chen Yu
title.raw: 《張耳陳餘列傳》 Biographies of Zhang Er and Chen Yu

sentences.zh: 張耳者，大梁人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Er was a person from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er was a native of Daliang.

sentences.zh: 其少時，及魏公子毋忌為客。

translations.literal: In his youth, he was a retainer of the Wei prince Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, he served as a retainer to Lord Xinling of Wei.

sentences.zh: 張耳嘗亡命游外黃。

translations.literal: Zhang Er once fled for his life and traveled to Waihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er once fled as a fugitive and wandered to Waihuang.

sentences.zh: 外黃富人女甚美，嫁庸奴，亡其夫，去抵父客。

translations.literal: A rich man's daughter in Waihuang was very beautiful; she had married a common slave, but her husband died, and she went to stay with a guest of her father.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man's daughter in Waihuang was a great beauty. She had been married to a worthless man, but after her husband died, she went to lodge with one of her father's guests.

sentences.zh: 父客素知張耳，乃謂女曰：「必欲求賢夫，從張耳。」

translations.literal: The father's guest had long known Zhang Er, and so he said to the woman: 'If you truly wish to find a worthy husband, follow Zhang Er.'
translations.idiomatic: This guest had long been acquainted with Zhang Er, and he told the woman, 'If you want a husband of true worth, then marry Zhang Er.'

sentences.zh: 女聽，乃卒為請決，嫁之張耳。

translations.literal: The woman agreed, and he finally arranged the matter and married her to Zhang Er.
translations.idiomatic: The woman consented, and the guest arranged everything and wed her to Zhang Er.

sentences.zh: 張耳是時脫身游，女家厚奉給張耳，張耳以故致千里客。

translations.literal: Zhang Er at that time was wandering freely; the woman's family generously provided for Zhang Er, and Zhang Er thereby attracted guests from a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er was then a wandering adventurer. His wife's family lavished resources upon him, and with these means he attracted followers from a thousand li around.

sentences.zh: 乃宦魏為外黃令。

translations.literal: He then entered service in Wei and became the Magistrate of Waihuang.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered the service of Wei and was appointed Magistrate of Waihuang.

sentences.zh: 名由此益賢。

translations.literal: His reputation thus grew ever more worthy.
translations.idiomatic: His fame grew steadily as a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 陳餘者，亦大梁人也，好儒術，數游趙苦陘。

translations.literal: Chen Yu was also a person from Daliang; he was fond of Confucian learning and frequently traveled to Kuxing in Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu was also a native of Daliang. He was devoted to Confucian learning and often traveled to Kuxing in the state of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 富人公乘氏以其女妻之，亦知陳餘非庸人也。

translations.literal: A rich man of the Gongcheng clan gave him his daughter in marriage, also knowing that Chen Yu was no ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: A wealthy man of the Gongcheng clan gave him his daughter in marriage, recognizing that Chen Yu was no ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 餘年少，父事張耳，兩人相與為刎頸交。

translations.literal: Yu was younger, and he served Zhang Er as a father; the two became sworn brothers willing to die for each other.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu was the younger of the two and looked up to Zhang Er as a father. Together they became the closest of friends, each willing to die for the other.

sentences.zh: 秦之滅大梁也，張耳家外黃。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed Daliang, Zhang Er's home was in Waihuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin destroyed Daliang, Zhang Er was living in Waihuang.

sentences.zh: 高祖為布衣時，嘗數從張耳游，客數月。

translations.literal: When the future Emperor Gaozu was still a commoner, he once stayed with Zhang Er several times, lodging for several months.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Gaozu was still a commoner, he visited Zhang Er on several occasions and stayed as his guest for months at a time.

sentences.zh: 秦滅魏數歲，已聞此兩人魏之名士也，購求有得張耳千金，陳餘五百金。

translations.literal: Several years after Qin destroyed Wei, having heard that these two men were famous gentlemen of Wei, it offered a reward of a thousand gold for capturing Zhang Er and five hundred gold for Chen Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Some years after Qin conquered Wei, word reached the court that these two men were celebrated figures of the former state. Qin posted bounties of a thousand gold pieces for Zhang Er and five hundred for Chen Yu.

sentences.zh: 張耳、陳餘乃變名姓，俱之陳，為里監門以自食。

translations.literal: Zhang Er and Chen Yu then changed their names and surnames, both went to Chen, and became village gate-watchers to feed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and Chen Yu assumed false names and fled together to the city of Chen, where they took positions as village gatekeepers to earn their keep.

sentences.zh: 兩人相對。

translations.literal: The two men stood facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: The two stood opposite each other at the gate.

sentences.zh: 里吏嘗有過笞陳餘，陳餘欲起，張耳躡之，使受笞。

translations.literal: A village official once came by and flogged Chen Yu for some offense; Chen Yu was about to rise up, but Zhang Er stepped on his foot and made him endure the flogging.
translations.idiomatic: Once, a village official flogged Chen Yu for some petty infraction. Chen Yu was about to leap up in fury, but Zhang Er trod on his foot and forced him to endure the beating.

sentences.zh: 吏去，張耳乃引陳餘之桑下而數之曰：「始吾與公言何如？

translations.literal: After the official left, Zhang Er led Chen Yu under a mulberry tree and rebuked him, saying: 'What did I say to you at the beginning?
translations.idiomatic: After the official had gone, Zhang Er pulled Chen Yu under a mulberry tree and rebuked him. 'What did I tell you at the start?

sentences.zh: 今見小辱而欲死一吏乎？」

translations.literal: Now you face a small humiliation and want to fight a petty official to the death?'
translations.idiomatic: Would you throw your life away over a petty official's insult?'

sentences.zh: 陳餘然之。

translations.literal: Chen Yu agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu acknowledged he was right.

sentences.zh: 秦詔書購求兩人，兩人亦反用門者以令里中。

translations.literal: Qin issued edicts offering bounties for the two men, but the two men in turn used their position as gatekeepers to give orders within the village.
translations.idiomatic: Even as Qin circulated warrants for their arrest, the two men turned their role as gatekeepers to their advantage, exercising authority over the village.

sentences.zh: 陳涉起蘄，至入陳，兵數萬。

translations.literal: Chen She rose in revolt at Qi, and by the time he entered Chen, he had tens of thousands of soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen She raised his rebellion at Qi and marched into the city of Chen, he commanded an army of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 張耳、陳餘上謁陳涉。

translations.literal: Zhang Er and Chen Yu went up to pay their respects to Chen She.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and Chen Yu went to present themselves before Chen She.

sentences.zh: 涉及左右生平數聞張耳、陳餘賢，未嘗見，見即大喜。

translations.literal: Chen She and those around him had long heard of the worthiness of Zhang Er and Chen Yu but had never met them; upon meeting them, they were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chen She and his attendants had heard for years of the fame and virtue of Zhang Er and Chen Yu, though they had never met in person. When they finally did, Chen She was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 陳中豪傑父老乃說陳涉曰：「將軍身被堅執銳，率士卒以誅暴秦，復立楚社稷，存亡繼絕，功德宜為王。

translations.literal: The heroes and elders in Chen then persuaded Chen She, saying: 'The General has personally donned armor and taken up weapons, led soldiers to punish the tyrannical Qin, restored the altars of Chu, preserved the fallen and continued the broken line. Such merit deserves to be king.
translations.idiomatic: The local leaders and elders of Chen urged Chen She, 'General, you have donned armor and taken up the blade, leading your soldiers to punish the tyranny of Qin. You have restored the altars of Chu and revived what was lost. Such deeds merit nothing less than the title of king.

sentences.zh: 且夫監臨天下諸將，不為王不可，願將軍立為楚王也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to oversee all the generals in the realm, one cannot do so without being king. We wish the General to be established as King of Chu.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to command all the generals under heaven, you must take the royal title. We beg you to proclaim yourself King of Chu.'

sentences.zh: 陳涉問此兩人，兩人對曰：「夫秦為無道，破人國家，滅人社稷，絕人後世，罷百姓之力，盡百姓之財。

translations.literal: Chen She asked these two men, and the two replied: 'Qin has been without the Way, destroying people's states, extinguishing their altars, cutting off their posterity, exhausting the people's strength, and draining the people's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Chen She consulted the two men, and they replied, 'Qin has ruled without righteousness. It destroyed other states, toppled their altars, severed their lines of succession, exhausted the strength of the common people, and drained their wealth.

sentences.zh: 將軍瞋目張膽，出萬死不顧一生之計，為天下除殘也。

translations.literal: The General opened his eyes wide and mustered his courage, going out into ten thousand deaths without concern for his single life, to rid the realm of cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: You, General, widened your eyes and steeled your courage, braving ten thousand deaths without a thought for your own life, all to rid the world of this tyranny.

sentences.zh: 今始至陳而王之，示天下私。

translations.literal: Now, having just arrived at Chen, you declare yourself king—this shows selfish intent to all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if you declare yourself king the moment you arrive at Chen, you will appear selfish in the eyes of the world.

sentences.zh: 願將軍毋王，急引兵而西，遣人立六國後，自為樹黨，為秦益敵也。

translations.literal: We wish the General would not take the title of king, but quickly lead his troops west, and send men to restore the descendants of the six states, thereby building alliances for himself and creating more enemies for Qin.
translations.idiomatic: We urge you not to claim the royal title. Instead, march your forces west at once and send envoys to restore the heirs of the six fallen states. In this way you will build a network of allies and multiply the enemies ranged against Qin.

sentences.zh: 敵多則力分，與眾則兵彊。

translations.literal: When enemies are many, their forces are divided; when allies are many, one's army is strong.
translations.idiomatic: The more enemies Qin faces, the thinner its forces will be spread; the more allies you gather, the mightier your army will grow.

sentences.zh: 如此野無交兵，縣無守城，誅暴秦，據咸陽以令諸侯。

translations.literal: In this way, there will be no battles in the open, no defended cities, and you will punish the tyrannical Qin, seize Xianyang, and command the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Then there will be no armies to fight in the field, no cities to besiege. You will destroy the Qin tyranny, occupy Xianyang, and issue commands to the lords of the realm.

sentences.zh: 諸侯亡而得立，以德服之，如此則帝業成矣。

translations.literal: The feudal lords who had perished will be restored; if you win them over with virtue, then the imperial enterprise will be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The lords whose states were destroyed will owe their restoration to you. Win them over through virtue, and the foundation of an empire will be laid.

sentences.zh: 今獨王陳，恐天下解也。」

translations.literal: If you now merely become king in Chen alone, we fear the realm will lose heart.'
translations.idiomatic: But if you simply set yourself up as king here in Chen, we fear the world's resolve will slacken.'

sentences.zh: 陳涉不聽，遂立為王。

translations.literal: Chen She did not listen, and thereupon established himself as king.
translations.idiomatic: Chen She did not heed their counsel and proclaimed himself king.

sentences.zh: 陳餘乃復說陳王曰：「大王舉梁、楚而西，務在入關，未及收河北也。

translations.literal: Chen Yu then further persuaded King Chen, saying: 'Your Majesty has raised Liang and Chu and marched west, with the priority of entering the Pass, without yet having taken the lands north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu then addressed King Chen again: 'Your Majesty has rallied the forces of Liang and Chu and pressed westward, focused on entering the Pass. But you have not yet secured the territory north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗游趙，知其豪桀及地形，願請奇兵北略趙地。」

translations.literal: Your servant has previously traveled in Zhao and knows its heroes and terrain. I wish to request a force of picked troops to go north and conquer the land of Zhao.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has traveled through Zhao and knows its leading men and its terrain. Grant me a detachment of picked troops, and I will march north to take the land of Zhao.'

sentences.zh: 於是陳王以故所善陳人武臣為將軍，邵騷為護軍，以張耳、陳餘為左右校尉，予卒三千人，北略趙地。

translations.literal: Thereupon King Chen appointed wuchen, a man of Chen whom he had long favored, as general, Shao Sao as protector of the army, and Zhang Er and Chen Yu as left and right colonels, giving them three thousand soldiers to go north and conquer the land of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen accordingly appointed his old friend Wu Chen, a native of Chen, as general, with Shao Sao as protector of the army and Zhang Er and Chen Yu as colonels of the left and right. He gave them three thousand soldiers and sent them north to conquer the land of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 武臣等從白馬渡河，至諸縣，說其豪桀曰：「秦為亂政虐刑以殘賊天下，數十年矣。

translations.literal: wuchen and the others crossed the Yellow River at Baima, went to the various counties, and persuaded their local heroes, saying: 'Qin has used chaotic governance and cruel punishments to ravage the world for decades.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chen and his officers crossed the Yellow River at Baima and visited the counties along their route, rallying the local leaders with these words: 'For decades, Qin has tyrannized the realm with misrule and savage punishments.

sentences.zh: 北有長城之役，南有五嶺之戍，外內騷動，百姓罷敝，頭會箕斂，以供軍費，財匱力盡，民不聊生。

translations.literal: In the north there is the labor of the Great Wall, in the south the garrison at the Five Ridges; within and without there is unrest, the people are exhausted, taxes are levied head by head and swept up like grain, to supply military expenses, wealth is depleted and strength exhausted, and the people cannot sustain their lives.
translations.idiomatic: In the north, the people toil on the Great Wall; in the south, they garrison the Five Ridges. The whole realm is in turmoil. The people are worn out, taxed head by head, their wealth swept up to fund the army until nothing remains, and they can no longer survive.

sentences.zh: 重之以苛法峻刑，使天下父子不相安。

translations.literal: On top of this, harsh laws and severe punishments are imposed, so that fathers and sons throughout the realm cannot live in peace with one another.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this, harsh laws and cruel punishments weigh upon them, until fathers and sons can no longer live together in peace.

sentences.zh: 陳王奮臂為天下倡始，王楚之地，方二千里，莫不響應，家自為怒，人自為鬬，各報其怨而攻其讎，縣殺其令丞，郡殺其守尉。

translations.literal: King Chen raised his arm to lead the world in revolt, claiming the land of Chu, an area of two thousand li square. None did not respond; every household was filled with rage, every person took up arms, each avenging their own grudges and attacking their enemies, with counties killing their magistrates and vice-magistrates, commanderies killing their governors and commandants.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen raised his arm and led the world in revolt, claiming the land of Chu across two thousand li. All responded to his call. Every household burned with anger, every man took up arms, each one avenging old grudges—killing county magistrates and commandery governors alike.

sentences.zh: 今已張大楚，王陳，使吳廣、周文將卒百萬西擊秦。

translations.literal: Now he has already expanded Chu greatly, established his capital at Chen, and sent Wu Guang and Zhou Wen to lead a million soldiers west to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He has already expanded the domain of Chu, established his court at Chen, and dispatched Wu Guang and Zhou Wen to lead a million soldiers west against Qin.

sentences.zh: 於此時而不成封侯之業者，非人豪也。

translations.literal: At such a time, anyone who does not seize the opportunity to become an enfeoffed lord is no hero.
translations.idiomatic: Any man who fails to seize this moment and win a lordship for himself is no hero.

sentences.zh: 諸君試相與計之！

translations.literal: Gentlemen, try to plan together!
translations.idiomatic: Consider this together, gentlemen!

sentences.zh: 夫天下同心而苦秦久矣。

translations.literal: The whole realm is of one mind and has suffered under Qin for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The whole world is united in its resentment of Qin, and has suffered under its yoke for far too long.

sentences.zh: 因天下之力而攻無道之君，報父兄之怨而成割地有土之業，此士之一時也。」

translations.literal: To harness the strength of the realm to attack a lawless ruler, to avenge the grievances of fathers and brothers while carving out one's own domain—this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for a man of ambition.'
translations.idiomatic: To harness the strength of the world to bring down a tyrant, to avenge the wrongs done to our fathers and brothers while carving out a domain of our own—this is the chance of a lifetime.'

sentences.zh: 豪桀皆然其言。

translations.literal: The local heroes all agreed with his words.
translations.idiomatic: The local leaders all agreed with his words.

sentences.zh: 乃行收兵，得數萬人，號武臣為武信君。

translations.literal: They then went about gathering troops, obtained tens of thousands of men, and gave wuchen the title Lord of Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: They marched on, rallying troops as they went, and gathered tens of thousands of men. Wu Chen was given the title Lord of Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 下趙十城，餘皆城守，莫肯下。

translations.literal: They took ten cities in Zhao; the rest all held their walls and refused to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They captured ten cities in Zhao, but the rest fortified their walls and refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 乃引兵東北擊范陽。

translations.literal: They then led their troops northeast to attack Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: They then led their army northeast to attack Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 范陽人蒯通說范陽令曰：「竊聞公之將死，故弔。

translations.literal: Kuai Tong, a man of Fanyang, persuaded the Magistrate of Fanyang, saying: 'I have privately heard that you are about to die, and so I have come to offer my condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Tong, a native of Fanyang, went to the magistrate and said, 'I have heard that you are about to die, so I have come to offer my condolences.

sentences.zh: 雖然，賀公得通而生。」

translations.literal: However, I also congratulate you on meeting me, Tong, and thus being able to live.'
translations.idiomatic: And yet I also congratulate you—for by meeting me, you may yet survive.'

sentences.zh: 范陽令曰：「何以弔之？」

translations.literal: The Magistrate of Fanyang said: 'Why do you offer condolences?'
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate asked, 'Why do you offer condolences?'

sentences.zh: 對曰：「秦法重，足下為范陽令十年矣，殺人之父，孤人之子，斷人之足，黥人之首，不可勝數。

translations.literal: He replied: 'The laws of Qin are severe. You have been Magistrate of Fanyang for ten years; you have killed people's fathers, orphaned their sons, amputated their feet, and tattooed their faces—too many to count.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Tong replied, 'The laws of Qin are brutal. You have been magistrate of Fanyang for ten years. You have put fathers to death, left children orphans, amputated feet, and branded faces—the victims are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 然而慈父孝子莫敢倳刃公之腹中者，畏秦法耳。

translations.literal: Yet the reason that loving fathers and filial sons have not dared to plunge a blade into your belly is simply that they feared the laws of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The only reason that loving fathers and dutiful sons have not yet plunged a blade into your belly is their fear of Qin's laws.

sentences.zh: 今天下大亂，秦法不施，然則慈父孝子且倳刃公之腹中以成其名，此臣之所以弔公也。

translations.literal: Now the realm is in great turmoil and the laws of Qin are no longer enforced; therefore, loving fathers and filial sons will plunge a blade into your belly to make their name. This is why I offer you my condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is in chaos and Qin's laws no longer hold. Those grieving fathers and sons will thrust a blade into your belly to win fame for themselves. That is why I offer my condolences.

sentences.zh: 今諸侯畔秦矣，武信君兵且至，而君堅守范陽，少年皆爭殺君，下武信君。

translations.literal: Now the feudal lords have rebelled against Qin, the forces of the Lord of Wuxin are approaching, and yet you stubbornly hold Fanyang; the young men will all vie to kill you and surrender to the Lord of Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: The lords have already turned against Qin, and the army of the Lord of Wuxin is nearly at your gates. If you stubbornly defend Fanyang, the young men of the city will fight one another for the honor of killing you and presenting your head to the Lord of Wuxin.

sentences.zh: 君急遣臣見武信君，可轉禍為福，在今矣。」

translations.literal: You must quickly send me to see the Lord of Wuxin; you can turn disaster into fortune—the time is now.'
translations.idiomatic: Send me to the Lord of Wuxin at once. You can still turn disaster into fortune, but only if you act now.'

sentences.zh: 范陽令乃使蒯通見武信君曰：「足下必將戰勝然後略地，攻得然後下城，臣竊以為過矣。

translations.literal: The Magistrate of Fanyang then sent Kuai Tong to see the Lord of Wuxin. Kuai Tong said: 'My lord, you insist on winning battles before taking territory, and on storming cities before they surrender. I humbly think this is a mistake.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Fanyang accordingly sent Kuai Tong to see the Lord of Wuxin. Kuai Tong said, 'My lord, your strategy is to win battles before claiming territory and to storm cities before accepting their surrender. With all respect, I believe this is an error.

sentences.zh: 誠聽臣之計，可不攻而降城，不戰而略地，傳檄而千里定，可乎？」

translations.literal: If you truly heed my plan, you can take cities without attacking, seize territory without fighting, and pacify a thousand li by sending dispatches—would that not be better?'
translations.idiomatic: If you heed my counsel, you can take cities without a siege, claim territory without a battle, and pacify a thousand li with nothing more than dispatches. Would that not be better?'

sentences.zh: 武信君曰：「何謂也？」

translations.literal: The Lord of Wuxin said: 'What do you mean?'
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Wuxin asked, 'What do you mean?'

sentences.zh: 蒯通曰：「今范陽令宜整頓其士卒以守戰者也，怯而畏死，貪而重富貴，故欲先天下降，畏君以為秦所置吏，誅殺如前十城也。

translations.literal: Kuai Tong said: 'The Magistrate of Fanyang should by rights rally his soldiers to defend and fight. But he is cowardly and fears death, greedy and prizes wealth and rank, so he wishes to be the first in the realm to surrender. He fears only that you will treat him as a Qin-appointed official and execute him as you did the magistrates of the ten cities before.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai Tong said, 'The magistrate of Fanyang ought to marshal his troops and fight. But he is a coward who fears death and a greedy man who craves wealth and rank. He longs to be the first to surrender, but fears that you will treat him as a Qin official and execute him as you did the magistrates of the last ten cities.

sentences.zh: 然今范陽少年亦方殺其令，自以城距君。

translations.literal: But at the same time, the young men of Fanyang are also about to kill their magistrate and use the city to resist you.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile, the young hotheads of Fanyang are on the verge of killing the magistrate themselves and using the city to resist you.

sentences.zh: 君何不齎臣侯印，拜范陽令，范陽令則以城下君，少年亦不敢殺其令。

translations.literal: Why not give me a lord's seal to bestow upon the Magistrate of Fanyang? Then the magistrate will surrender the city to you, and the young men will not dare to kill their magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Why not give me a lord's seal to bestow upon the magistrate? He will surrender the city to you at once, and the young men will not dare to lay a hand on him.

sentences.zh: 令范陽令乘朱輪華轂，使驅馳燕、趙郊。

translations.literal: Then let the Magistrate of Fanyang ride in a carriage with vermilion wheels and ornate hubs, and have him drive about the outskirts of Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Then let the magistrate ride forth in a carriage with vermilion wheels and gilded hubs, parading through the borderlands of Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 燕、趙郊見之，皆曰此范陽令，先下者也，即喜矣，燕、趙城可毋戰而降也。

translations.literal: When the people of the Yan and Zhao borderlands see him, they will all say, 'This is the Magistrate of Fanyang, the first to surrender,' and they will be glad; the cities of Yan and Zhao can then surrender without a fight.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Yan and Zhao see him, they will say, "That is the magistrate of Fanyang, the first to submit," and they will rejoice. The cities of Yan and Zhao will then surrender without a fight.

sentences.zh: 此臣之所謂傳檄而千里定者也。」

translations.literal: This is what I meant by pacifying a thousand li by sending dispatches.'
translations.idiomatic: This is what I meant by pacifying a thousand li with dispatches alone.'

sentences.zh: 武信君從其計，因使蒯通賜范陽令侯印。

translations.literal: The Lord of Wuxin followed his plan and sent Kuai Tong to bestow a lord's seal upon the Magistrate of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Wuxin adopted his plan and sent Kuai Tong to bestow a lord's seal upon the magistrate of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 趙地聞之，不戰以城下者三十餘城。

translations.literal: When the land of Zhao heard of this, more than thirty cities surrendered without a fight.
translations.idiomatic: When word of this spread through the land of Zhao, more than thirty cities surrendered without a fight.

sentences.zh: 至邯鄲，張耳、陳餘聞周章軍入關，至戲卻；

translations.literal: When they reached Handan, Zhang Er and Chen Yu heard that Zhou Zhang's army had entered the Pass and advanced to Xi, but then been driven back;
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Handan, Zhang Er and Chen Yu received word that the army of Zhou Zhang had entered the Pass and advanced as far as Xi before being driven back.

sentences.zh: 又聞諸將為陳王徇地，多以讒毀得罪誅，怨陳王不其筴不以為將而以為校尉。

translations.literal: They also heard that many generals who had conquered territory for King Chen had been slandered and executed; they resented King Chen for not following their advice and for making them colonels instead of generals.
translations.idiomatic: They also heard that many of the generals who had conquered territory for King Chen had been slandered and put to death. They resented King Chen for ignoring their counsel and for appointing them merely as colonels rather than generals.

sentences.zh: 乃說武臣曰：「陳王起蘄，至陳而王，非必立六國後。

translations.literal: They then persuaded Wu Chen, saying: 'King Chen rose at Qi, arrived at Chen and made himself king, without necessarily restoring the descendants of the six states.
translations.idiomatic: They then spoke to Wu Chen: 'King Chen rose in revolt at Qi and proclaimed himself king at Chen without bothering to restore the heirs of the six states.

sentences.zh: 將軍今以三千人下趙數十城，獨介居河北，不王無以填之。

translations.literal: General, you have now taken dozens of Zhao cities with three thousand men and stand alone north of the Yellow River; without becoming king, there is no way to hold all this.
translations.idiomatic: You, General, have taken dozens of cities in Zhao with only three thousand men and now hold a vast territory north of the Yellow River. Without the title of king, you cannot hold it together.

sentences.zh: 且陳王聽讒，還報，恐不脫於禍。

translations.literal: Moreover, King Chen heeds slander; if you return to report, you may not escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, King Chen heeds slander. If you go back to report to him, you may well not escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 又不如立其兄弟；

translations.literal: It would be better to establish one of his brothers;
translations.idiomatic: Better to establish one of his brothers as king;

sentences.zh: 不，即立趙後。

translations.literal: if not, then establish a descendant of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: or failing that, restore a descendant of the royal house of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 將軍毋失時，時閒不容息。」

translations.literal: General, do not lose the moment—there is not a breath of time to spare.'
translations.idiomatic: General, do not let this moment slip away. There is not a breath of time to spare.'

sentences.zh: 武臣乃聽之，遂立為趙王。

translations.literal: Wu Chen then heeded their advice and thereupon established himself as King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chen heeded their counsel and proclaimed himself King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 以陳餘為大將軍，張耳為右丞相，邵騷為左丞相。

translations.literal: He appointed Chen Yu as Grand General, Zhang Er as Right Chancellor, and Shao Sao as Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu was made Grand General, Zhang Er Right Chancellor, and Shao Sao Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 使人報陳王，陳王大怒，欲盡族武臣等家，而發兵擊趙。

translations.literal: They sent someone to report to King Chen. King Chen was furious and wished to exterminate the clans of Wu Chen and the others and to send troops to attack Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached King Chen, he was furious. He wanted to exterminate the families of Wu Chen and the others and send an army to attack Zhao.

sentences.zh: 陳王相國房君諫曰：「秦未亡而誅武臣等家，此又生一秦也。

translations.literal: King Chen's Chancellor, Lord Fang, remonstrated, saying: 'Qin has not yet fallen, and if you execute the families of Wu Chen and the others, you will merely create another Qin.
translations.idiomatic: His chancellor, Lord Fang, remonstrated: 'Qin has not yet fallen. If you execute the families of Wu Chen and his companions, you will only create another Qin.

sentences.zh: 不如因而賀之，使急引兵西擊秦。」

translations.literal: It would be better to congratulate them and order them to quickly lead their troops west to attack Qin.'
translations.idiomatic: Better to congratulate them and order them to march their forces west against Qin at once.'

sentences.zh: 陳王然之，從其計，徙系武臣等家宮中，封張耳子敖為成都君。

translations.literal: King Chen agreed, followed his plan, moved the families of Wu Chen and the others into the palace under house arrest, and enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Ao as Lord of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen agreed and adopted this plan. He moved the families of Wu Chen and the others into the palace as hostages and enfeoffed Zhang Er's son Zhang Ao as Lord of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 陳王使使者賀趙，令趣發兵西入關。

translations.literal: King Chen sent envoys to congratulate Zhao and ordered them to quickly send troops west to enter the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: King Chen dispatched envoys to congratulate the King of Zhao and urge him to send his forces west through the Pass at once.

sentences.zh: 張耳、陳餘說武臣曰：「王王趙，非楚意，特以計賀王。

translations.literal: Zhang Er and Chen Yu persuaded Wu Chen, saying: 'Your becoming King of Zhao was not Chu's true wish; they merely congratulated you as a stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and Chen Yu counseled Wu Chen: 'Your kingship over Zhao was never Chu's true desire. They congratulated you only as a matter of strategy.

sentences.zh: 楚已滅秦，必加兵於趙。

translations.literal: Once Chu has destroyed Qin, it will surely turn its army against Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chu has destroyed Qin, they will surely turn their armies against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 願王毋西兵，北徇燕、代，南收河內以自廣。

translations.literal: We wish the King would not send troops west, but instead go north to take Yan and Dai, and south to seize Henei, to expand his own territory.
translations.idiomatic: We urge Your Majesty not to send troops west. Instead, expand northward into Yan and Dai and southward to seize Henei, thereby strengthening your own position.

sentences.zh: 趙南據大河，北有燕、代，楚雖勝秦，必不敢制趙。」

translations.literal: With Zhao holding the Yellow River to the south and Yan and Dai to the north, even if Chu defeats Qin, it will surely not dare to subdue Zhao.'
translations.idiomatic: With the Yellow River guarding Zhao to the south and Yan and Dai to the north, even if Chu defeats Qin, it will never dare to challenge you.'

sentences.zh: 趙王以為然，因不西兵，而使韓廣略燕，李良略常山，張黡略上黨。

translations.literal: The King of Zhao agreed, and so he did not send troops west, but sent Han Guang to conquer Yan, Li Liang to conquer Changshan, and Zhang Yan to conquer Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao agreed. He did not send his troops west, but instead dispatched Han Guang to take Yan, Li Liang to take Changshan, and Zhang Yan to take Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 韓廣至燕，燕人因立廣為燕王。

translations.literal: When Han Guang reached Yan, the people of Yan established him as King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Guang arrived in Yan, the people of Yan made him their king.

sentences.zh: 趙王乃與張耳、陳餘北略地燕界。

translations.literal: The King of Zhao then went with Zhang Er and Chen Yu to conquer territory northward toward the Yan border.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao then marched north with Zhang Er and Chen Yu to seize territory along the Yan border.

sentences.zh: 趙王閒出，為燕軍所得。

translations.literal: The King of Zhao went out with a small escort and was captured by the Yan army.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao ventured out with a light escort and was captured by the army of Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕將囚之，欲與分趙地半，乃歸王。

translations.literal: The Yan generals imprisoned him and demanded half of Zhao's territory before they would return the king.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan generals held him prisoner and demanded half of Zhao's territory as the price of his return.

sentences.zh: 使者往，燕輒殺之以求地。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys went, Yan immediately killed them and pressed for territory.
translations.idiomatic: Every envoy sent to negotiate was killed by Yan, which continued to press its demands for territory.

sentences.zh: 張耳、陳餘患之。

translations.literal: Zhang Er and Chen Yu were deeply troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and Chen Yu were gravely troubled.

sentences.zh: 有廝養卒謝其舍中曰：「吾為公說燕，與趙王載歸。」

translations.literal: There was a camp servant who said farewell to his messmates, saying: 'I will go and persuade Yan for you, and bring the King of Zhao back in my carriage.'
translations.idiomatic: A lowly camp servant bid farewell to his companions and said, 'I will go and persuade Yan, and bring the King of Zhao home.'

sentences.zh: 舍中皆笑曰：「使者往十餘輩，輒死，若何以能得王？」

translations.literal: Everyone in the quarters laughed, saying: 'Over ten envoys have gone, and all have been killed. How can you possibly get the king back?'
translations.idiomatic: They all laughed at him. 'More than ten envoys have gone, and every one has been killed. What makes you think you can succeed?'

sentences.zh: 乃走燕壁。

translations.literal: He then ran to the Yan camp.
translations.idiomatic: But the servant went straight to the Yan camp.

sentences.zh: 燕將見之，問燕將曰：「知臣何欲？」

translations.literal: When the Yan general received him, the servant asked, 'Do you know what I want?'
translations.idiomatic: When he was brought before the Yan general, the servant asked, 'Do you know what I have come for?'

sentences.zh: 燕將曰：「若欲得趙王耳。」

translations.literal: The Yan general said: 'You want to get the King of Zhao back.'
translations.idiomatic: The Yan general said, 'You want the King of Zhao returned.'

sentences.zh: 曰：「君知張耳、陳餘何如人也？」

translations.literal: He said: 'Do you know what kind of men Zhang Er and Chen Yu are?'
translations.idiomatic: The servant replied, 'Do you know what kind of men Zhang Er and Chen Yu are?'

sentences.zh: 燕將曰：「賢人也。」

translations.literal: The Yan general said: 'They are worthy men.'
translations.idiomatic: The general said, 'They are men of great ability.'

sentences.zh: 曰：「知其志何欲？」

translations.literal: The servant asked, 'Do you know what they truly desire?'
translations.idiomatic: The servant asked, 'And do you know what they truly desire?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「欲得其王耳。」

translations.literal: The Yan general said, 'They want to get their king back, that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: The Yan general replied, 'They want their king back, nothing more.'

sentences.zh: 趙養卒乃笑曰：「君未知此兩人所欲也。

translations.literal: The Zhao camp servant then laughed, saying: 'You do not understand what these two men truly want.
translations.idiomatic: The servant laughed. 'You do not understand what those two men truly want.

sentences.zh: 夫武臣、張耳、陳餘杖馬箠下趙數十城，此亦各欲南面而王，豈欲為卿相終己邪？

translations.literal: Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu wielded riding crops and took dozens of Zhao cities; each of them wants to face south and rule as king—do you think they wish to remain ministers to the end of their days?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu conquered dozens of cities in Zhao with nothing but riding crops. Each of them wants to face south and rule as king. Do you really think they are content to remain ministers forever?

sentences.zh: 夫臣與主豈可同日而道哉，顧其勢初定，未敢參分而王，且以少長先立武臣為王，以持趙心。

translations.literal: How can minister and master be spoken of in the same breath? It is only that the situation has just been settled and they did not dare divide the land and make themselves kings; so for now, by seniority, they first established Wu Chen as king to hold the hearts of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: How can a minister be compared to a sovereign? It is simply that the situation was not yet settled, and they did not dare divide the territory among themselves. So they set up Wu Chen as king first, by seniority, to hold the loyalty of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 今趙地已服，此兩人亦欲分趙而王，時未可耳。

translations.literal: Now that the land of Zhao is subdued, these two men also wish to divide Zhao and make themselves kings—the time is simply not yet right.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Zhao is subdued, the two of them also wish to divide it and claim their own kingdoms. The time is simply not yet ripe.

sentences.zh: 今君乃囚趙王。

translations.literal: Now you have imprisoned the King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: And now you have imprisoned the King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 此兩人名為求趙王，實欲燕殺之，此兩人分趙自立。

translations.literal: These two men claim to be seeking the King of Zhao's return, but in reality they want Yan to kill him, so that the two of them can divide Zhao and set themselves up as kings.
translations.idiomatic: These two men claim they want the king returned, but in truth they hope Yan will kill him, so they can divide Zhao between themselves and each claim a throne.

sentences.zh: 夫以一趙尚易燕，況以兩賢王左提右挈，而責殺王之罪，滅燕易矣。」

translations.literal: Even a single Zhao could easily overpower Yan; how much more so when two capable kings join forces, using the crime of killing their king as a pretext—destroying Yan would be easy indeed.'
translations.idiomatic: A single Zhao could already overpower Yan. Imagine two capable kings joining forces, using the murder of their sovereign as their pretext for war. Destroying Yan would be child's play.'

sentences.zh: 燕將以為然，乃歸趙王，養卒為御而歸。

translations.literal: The Yan general thought this was right, and so returned the King of Zhao. The camp servant drove the carriage and brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan general was persuaded. He released the King of Zhao, and the camp servant drove the carriage that brought the king home.

sentences.zh: 李良已定常山，還報，趙王復使良略太原。

translations.literal: Li Liang had already pacified Changshan and returned to report. The King of Zhao then sent him again to take Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liang had already pacified Changshan and returned to report. The King of Zhao then sent him to take Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 至石邑，秦兵塞井陘，未能前。

translations.literal: When he reached Shiyi, the Qin army had blocked the Jingxing Pass, and he was unable to advance.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Shiyi, he found the Jingxing Pass blocked by Qin forces and was unable to advance.

sentences.zh: 秦將詐稱二世使人遺李良書，不封，曰：「良嘗事我得顯幸。

translations.literal: A Qin general then forged a letter as if from the Second Emperor to Li Liang, leaving it unsealed, which said: 'Liang once served me and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: A Qin general then forged a letter in the name of the Second Emperor and sent it to Li Liang, deliberately leaving it unsealed. It read: 'Liang once served me and won great favor.

sentences.zh: 良誠能反趙為秦，赦良罪，貴良。」

translations.literal: If Liang can truly turn against Zhao and serve Qin, Liang's crimes will be pardoned and Liang will be made noble.'
translations.idiomatic: If Liang truly turns against Zhao and serves Qin, his crimes shall be pardoned, and he shall be raised to high rank.'

sentences.zh: 良得書，疑不信。

translations.literal: When Liang received the letter, he was suspicious and did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Liang received the letter, he was suspicious and did not trust it.

sentences.zh: 乃還之邯鄲，益請兵。

translations.literal: He then returned to Handan to request more troops.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back toward Handan to request reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 未至，道逢趙王姊出飲，從百餘騎。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, on the road he encountered the King of Zhao's elder sister going out to a banquet, accompanied by over a hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Handan, he encountered the King of Zhao's elder sister on the road, heading out to a banquet with an escort of more than a hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 李良望見，以為王，伏謁道旁。

translations.literal: Li Liang saw her from afar, took the party for the king, and prostrated himself by the roadside in greeting.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liang saw the procession from a distance and, mistaking it for the king's retinue, prostrated himself at the roadside in greeting.

sentences.zh: 王姊醉，不知其將，使騎謝李良。

translations.literal: The king's sister was drunk and did not recognize him as a general; she merely sent a rider to dismiss Li Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The king's sister was drunk and did not recognize him as a general. She sent a rider to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 李良素貴，起，慚其從官。

translations.literal: Li Liang had always been a man of high standing; when he rose, he was humiliated before his own attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liang, accustomed to being treated with deference, rose to his feet mortified in front of his own officers.

sentences.zh: 從官有一人曰：「天下畔秦，能者先立。

translations.literal: One of his attendants said: 'The whole realm has rebelled against Qin; the capable are the first to establish themselves.
translations.idiomatic: One of his officers said, 'The whole realm has turned against Qin. The capable are the first to rise.

sentences.zh: 且趙王素出將軍下，今女兒乃不為將軍下車，請追殺之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the King of Zhao has always ranked below the General; now a mere woman refuses to dismount for the General. I beg you to pursue and kill her.'
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the King of Zhao himself has always ranked below you. Yet this woman did not even dismount from her carriage for you. I urge you to pursue her and put her to death.'

sentences.zh: 李良已得秦書，固欲反趙，未決，因此怒，遣人追殺王姊道中，乃遂將其兵襲邯鄲。

translations.literal: Li Liang had already received the Qin letter and had long wanted to turn against Zhao but had not yet decided. Because of this anger, he sent men to pursue and kill the king's sister on the road, and then led his troops in a surprise attack on Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liang had already received the Qin letter and had been inclined to betray Zhao, though he had not yet made up his mind. Now, in his fury, he sent men to pursue and kill the king's sister on the road, then led his troops in a surprise attack on Handan.

sentences.zh: 邯鄲不知，竟殺武臣、邵騷。

translations.literal: Handan was caught unawares, and in the end Wu Chen and Shao Sao were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Handan was caught completely off guard, and Wu Chen and Shao Sao were both killed.

sentences.zh: 趙人多為張耳、陳餘耳目者，以故得脫出。

translations.literal: Many people of Zhao served as eyes and ears for Zhang Er and Chen Yu, and so the two were able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Many among the people of Zhao served as informants for Zhang Er and Chen Yu, and thanks to their warnings the two men managed to escape.

sentences.zh: 收其兵，得數萬人。

translations.literal: They gathered troops and obtained tens of thousands of men.
translations.idiomatic: They rallied the scattered troops and assembled an army of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 客有說張耳曰：「兩君羈旅，而欲附趙，難；

translations.literal: A retainer persuaded Zhang Er, saying: 'You two are strangers here; it will be difficult to win Zhao's allegiance simply by attaching yourselves to it.
translations.idiomatic: One of their retainers counseled Zhang Er: 'You two are outsiders here. To win the allegiance of Zhao by your own authority alone will be difficult.

sentences.zh: 獨立趙後，扶以義，可就功。」

translations.literal: If instead you restore a descendant of the Zhao royal house and support him with righteousness, you can achieve great things.'
translations.idiomatic: But if you restore a descendant of the Zhao royal house and support him in the name of righteousness, you can achieve great things.'

sentences.zh: 乃求得趙歇，立為趙王，居信都。

translations.literal: They then found Zhao Xie and established him as King of Zhao, with his capital at Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: They searched out Zhao Xie, a scion of the old royal house, and established him as King of Zhao, with his court at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 李良進兵擊陳餘，陳餘敗李良，李良走歸章邯。

translations.literal: Li Liang advanced his troops to attack Chen Yu, but Chen Yu defeated Li Liang, and Li Liang fled to join Zhang Han.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liang advanced to attack Chen Yu, but Chen Yu defeated him. Li Liang fled and joined the Qin general Zhang Han.

sentences.zh: 章邯引兵至邯鄲，皆徙其民河內，夷其城郭。

translations.literal: Zhang Han then led his troops to Handan, relocated all its people to Henei, and razed its walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han led his forces to Handan, deported the entire population to Henei, and leveled the city walls.

sentences.zh: 張耳與趙王歇走入鉅鹿城，王離圍之。

translations.literal: Zhang Er and King Zhao Xie fled into the city of Julu. Wang Li laid siege to it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er and King Zhao Xie retreated into the city of Julu, where Wang Li besieged them.

sentences.zh: 陳餘北收常山兵，得數萬人，軍鉅鹿北。

translations.literal: Chen Yu went north to gather the troops of Changshan, obtained tens of thousands of men, and encamped north of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu marched north and gathered the troops of Changshan, assembling tens of thousands of men. He encamped to the north of Julu.

sentences.zh: 章邯軍鉅鹿南棘原，筑甬道屬河，餉王離。

translations.literal: Zhang Han encamped at Jiyuan, south of Julu, and built a walled supply corridor connecting to the river to provision Wang Li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han encamped at Jiyuan to the south of Julu and built a walled corridor to the river through which he supplied Wang Li with provisions.

sentences.zh: 王離兵食多，急攻鉅鹿。

translations.literal: Wang Li had abundant troops and supplies, and he pressed the attack on Julu.
translations.idiomatic: With ample troops and provisions, Wang Li pressed his assault on Julu relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 鉅鹿城中食盡兵少，張耳數使人召前陳餘，陳餘自度兵少，不敵秦，不敢前。

translations.literal: Inside Julu, food was exhausted and soldiers were few. Zhang Er repeatedly sent messengers to summon Chen Yu forward, but Chen Yu judged his forces too few to match Qin and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Julu, food had run out, and the garrison was thin. Zhang Er repeatedly sent messengers urging Chen Yu to come to their aid, but Chen Yu judged his forces too few to challenge Qin and did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 數月，張耳大怒，怨陳餘，使張黶、陳澤往讓陳餘曰：「始吾與公為刎頸交，今王與耳旦暮且死，而公擁兵數萬，不肯相救，安在其相為死！

translations.literal: After several months, Zhang Er was furious and resentful of Chen Yu. He sent Zhang Yan and Chen Ze to go and reproach Chen Yu, saying: 'In the beginning we swore to die for each other. Now the king and I face death any day, and yet you sit with tens of thousands of troops and refuse to come to our aid—where is your oath to die for me?
translations.idiomatic: After months of this, Zhang Er was consumed with fury and resentment toward Chen Yu. He sent Zhang Yan and Chen Ze to reproach him: 'We swore we would die for each other. Now the king and I face death at any moment, and yet you sit with tens of thousands of troops and refuse to come to our rescue. What has become of your oath?

sentences.zh: 茍必信，胡不赴秦軍俱死？

translations.literal: If you are truly faithful, why not charge the Qin army and die together with us?
translations.idiomatic: If your word still means anything, why not throw yourself against the Qin army and die alongside us?

sentences.zh: 且有十一二相全。」

translations.literal: Besides, there is perhaps a one or two in ten chance of saving each other.'
translations.idiomatic: At the very least, there is a chance—one in ten, perhaps—that together we might survive.'

sentences.zh: 陳餘曰：「吾度前終不能救趙，徒盡亡軍。

translations.literal: Chen Yu said: 'I judge that advancing would ultimately fail to save Zhao and would only destroy my entire army for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu replied, 'I have calculated the odds. Advancing now would not save Zhao—it would only destroy my entire army for nothing.

sentences.zh: 且餘所以不俱死，欲為趙王、張君報秦。

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason I do not die together with you is that I wish to avenge the King of Zhao and Lord Zhang against Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I do not throw my life away is that I still hope to avenge the King of Zhao and you, Lord Zhang, against Qin.

sentences.zh: 今必俱死，如以肉委餓虎，何益？」

translations.literal: To insist that we all die together now would be like throwing meat to a hungry tiger—what good would it do?'
translations.idiomatic: To insist that we all die together now would be like throwing meat to a starving tiger. What good would that do?'

sentences.zh: 張黶、陳澤曰：「事已急，要以俱死立信，安知後慮！」

translations.literal: Zhang Yan and Chen Ze said: 'The situation is desperate! You must die together with them to prove your faith. Who can think of future plans at a time like this!'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan and Chen Ze said, 'The situation is desperate. You must prove your faith by dying together with them. This is no time to think about the future!'

sentences.zh: 陳餘曰：「吾死顧以為無益。

translations.literal: Chen Yu said: 'I believe that my death would serve no purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu said, 'My death would accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 必如公言。」

translations.literal: But let it be as you say.'
translations.idiomatic: But let it be as you say.'

sentences.zh: 乃使五千人令張黶、陳澤先嘗秦軍，至皆沒。

translations.literal: He then sent five thousand men under Zhang Yan and Chen Ze to first test the Qin army; they advanced and were all wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Zhang Yan and Chen Ze five thousand men to probe the Qin lines. They advanced and were annihilated to the last man.

sentences.zh: 當是時，燕、齊、楚聞趙急，皆來救。

translations.literal: At that time, Yan, Qi, and Chu heard that Zhao was in dire straits and all came to its rescue.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, Yan, Qi, and Chu heard of Zhao's peril and all sent forces to its aid.

sentences.zh: 張敖亦北收代兵，得萬餘人，來，皆壁餘旁，未敢擊秦。

translations.literal: Zhang Ao also went north to gather troops from Dai, obtaining over ten thousand men. They came and all encamped beside Chen Yu, but none dared to attack Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ao likewise went north and gathered more than ten thousand troops from Dai. He arrived and encamped alongside Chen Yu, but like the others, none of them dared to engage the Qin forces.

sentences.zh: 項羽兵數絕章邯甬道，王離軍乏食，項羽悉引兵渡河，遂破章邯。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu's forces repeatedly severed Zhang Han's supply corridor. When Wang Li's army ran short of food, Xiang Yu led his entire army across the river and defeated Zhang Han.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu's forces repeatedly cut Zhang Han's supply corridor. When Wang Li's army began to run short of provisions, Xiang Yu led his entire army across the river and routed Zhang Han.

sentences.zh: 章邯引兵解，諸侯軍乃敢擊圍鉅鹿秦軍，遂虜王離。

translations.literal: Zhang Han withdrew his troops and retreated. Only then did the armies of the various lords dare to attack the Qin forces besieging Julu, and they captured Wang Li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han pulled back his forces in retreat. Only then did the armies of the other lords dare to attack the Qin troops besieging Julu, and they captured Wang Li.

sentences.zh: 涉閒自殺。

translations.literal: She Jian killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: She Jian took his own life.

sentences.zh: 卒存鉅鹿者，楚力也。

translations.literal: In the end, what saved Julu was the strength of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, it was the might of Chu that saved Julu.

sentences.zh: 於是趙王歇、張耳乃得出鉅鹿，謝諸侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon King Zhao Xie and Zhang Er were able to leave Julu and expressed their gratitude to the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao Xie and Zhang Er were finally able to leave Julu. They expressed their gratitude to the assembled lords.

sentences.zh: 張耳與陳餘相見，責讓陳餘以不肯救趙，及問張黶、陳澤所在。

translations.literal: When Zhang Er met with Chen Yu, he reproached Chen Yu for refusing to come to Zhao's rescue and asked where Zhang Yan and Chen Ze were.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Er met Chen Yu, he upbraided him for refusing to come to Zhao's rescue and demanded to know where Zhang Yan and Chen Ze were.

sentences.zh: 陳餘怒曰：「張黶、陳澤以必死責臣，臣使將五千人先嘗秦軍，皆沒不出。」

translations.literal: Chen Yu replied angrily: 'Zhang Yan and Chen Ze demanded that I die with them. I gave them five thousand men to probe the Qin army first, and they were all wiped out without a single man returning.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu replied angrily, 'Zhang Yan and Chen Ze demanded that I die alongside them. I gave them five thousand men to test the Qin lines, and every last one of them perished.'

sentences.zh: 張耳不信，以為殺之，數問陳餘。

translations.literal: Zhang Er did not believe him and suspected that he had killed them. He questioned Chen Yu repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er did not believe him. He suspected Chen Yu of having killed them and pressed him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 陳餘怒曰：「不意君之望臣深也！

translations.literal: Chen Yu said angrily: 'I did not expect that your resentment of me would run so deep!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu said in a fury, 'I never imagined your resentment toward me ran so deep!

sentences.zh: 豈以臣為重去將哉？」

translations.literal: Do you think I would sacrifice my generals because of my resentment toward you?'
translations.idiomatic: Do you think I would sacrifice my generals out of spite toward you?'

sentences.zh: 乃脫解印綬，推予張耳。

translations.literal: He then unfastened his seal and ribbon and pushed them toward Zhang Er.
translations.idiomatic: He tore off his seal of office and thrust it toward Zhang Er.

sentences.zh: 張耳亦愕不受。

translations.literal: Zhang Er was also startled and did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er was taken aback and refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 陳餘起如廁。

translations.literal: Chen Yu rose and went to the privy.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu rose and left to use the privy.

sentences.zh: 客有說張耳曰：「臣聞『天與不取，反受其咎』。

translations.literal: A retainer persuaded Zhang Er, saying: "I have heard the saying, 'When Heaven gives and you do not take, you will suffer the consequences.'
translations.idiomatic: A retainer urged Zhang Er: "I have heard the saying, 'Refuse a gift from Heaven, and you will suffer for your refusal.'

sentences.zh: 今陳將軍與君印，君不受，反天不祥。

translations.literal: Now General Chen has offered you his seal, and you refuse it—to defy Heaven is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: General Chen has offered you his seal of command. If you refuse it, you defy Heaven, and that will bring misfortune.

sentences.zh: 急取之！」

translations.literal: Take it quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: Take it at once!"

sentences.zh: 張耳乃佩其印，收其麾下。

translations.literal: Zhang Er then wore the seal and took command of Chen Yu's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er put on the seal and took command of Chen Yu's forces.

sentences.zh: 而陳餘還，亦望張耳不讓，遂趨出。

translations.literal: When Chen Yu returned, he was also resentful that Zhang Er had not declined, and he hastened out.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yu returned and saw that Zhang Er had not refused the seal, he was filled with resentment and stormed out.

sentences.zh: 張耳遂收其兵。

translations.literal: Zhang Er thereupon took over his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er thereupon absorbed all of Chen Yu's troops.

sentences.zh: 陳餘獨與麾下所善數百人之河上澤中漁獵。

translations.literal: Chen Yu went alone with a few hundred trusted followers to fish and hunt in the marshes along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu departed with only a few hundred loyal followers and went to fish and hunt in the marshes along the river.

sentences.zh: 由此陳餘、張耳遂有卻。

translations.literal: From this point on, Chen Yu and Zhang Er became estranged.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, the rift between Chen Yu and Zhang Er became irreparable.

sentences.zh: 趙王歇復居信都。

translations.literal: King Zhao Xie once again resided in Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao Xie returned to his capital at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 張耳從項羽諸侯入關。

translations.literal: Zhang Er followed Xiang Yu and the other lords through the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er accompanied Xiang Yu and the other lords through the Pass into the heartland of Qin.

sentences.zh: 漢元年二月，項羽立諸侯王，張耳雅游，人多為之言，項羽亦素數聞張耳賢，乃分趙立張耳為常山王，治信都。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Han, Xiang Yu enfeoffed the feudal kings. Zhang Er had many distinguished connections, and many people spoke on his behalf. Xiang Yu had also long heard of Zhang Er's worthiness, so he divided Zhao and established Zhang Er as King of Changshan, governing from Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Han, Xiang Yu divided the realm and enfeoffed the lords as kings. Zhang Er was well-connected, and many spoke on his behalf. Xiang Yu himself had long heard of Zhang Er's reputation, so he carved off part of Zhao and made Zhang Er King of Changshan, with his capital at Xindu.

sentences.zh: 信都更名襄國。

translations.literal: Xindu was renamed Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: The capital at Xindu was given the new name Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 陳餘客多說項羽曰：「陳餘、張耳一體有功於趙。」

translations.literal: Many of Chen Yu's retainers spoke to Xiang Yu, saying: 'Chen Yu and Zhang Er rendered service to Zhao as one body.'
translations.idiomatic: Many of Chen Yu's retainers petitioned Xiang Yu, saying, "Chen Yu and Zhang Er served Zhao as partners with equal merit."

sentences.zh: 項羽以陳餘不從入關，聞其在南皮，即以南皮旁三縣以封之，而徙趙王歇王代。

translations.literal: Since Chen Yu had not followed him through the Pass, Xiang Yu, hearing that he was at Nanpi, enfeoffed him with the three counties around Nanpi, and transferred King Zhao Xie to be King of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: But because Chen Yu had not accompanied the army through the Pass, Xiang Yu only granted him three counties around Nanpi, where he was residing. He transferred King Zhao Xie to rule as King of Dai.

sentences.zh: 張耳之國，陳餘愈益怒，曰：「張耳與餘功等也，今張耳王，餘獨侯，此項羽不平。」

translations.literal: When Zhang Er went to his kingdom, Chen Yu grew even more furious, saying: 'Zhang Er's achievements and mine are equal, yet now Zhang Er is a king while I am merely a marquis. Xiang Yu is unjust.'
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Er departed for his kingdom, Chen Yu's anger deepened. 'Zhang Er and I rendered equal service,' he said. 'Yet Zhang Er is made a king while I receive a mere marquisate. Xiang Yu's judgment is unjust.'

sentences.zh: 及齊王田榮畔楚，陳餘乃使夏說說田榮曰：「項羽為天下宰不平，盡王諸將善地，徙故王王惡地，今趙王乃居代！

translations.literal: When the King of Qi, Tian Rong, rebelled against Chu, Chen Yu sent Xia Yue to persuade Tian Rong, saying: 'Xiang Yu rules the world unjustly. He has made all his generals kings of the best lands while relocating the former kings to poor lands. Now the King of Zhao has been banished to Dai!
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Rong, the King of Qi, rebelled against Chu, Chen Yu sent Xia Yue to Tian Rong with this message: 'Xiang Yu has divided the realm unjustly. He grants the best territories to his own generals and banishes the rightful kings to wasteland. The King of Zhao has been exiled to Dai!

sentences.zh: 願王假臣兵，請以南皮為捍蔽。」

translations.literal: I beg the King to lend me troops, and I will use Nanpi as a shield for your border.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to lend me troops. I will use Nanpi as a bulwark to shield your border.'

sentences.zh: 田榮欲樹黨於趙以反楚，乃遣兵從陳餘。

translations.literal: Tian Rong wished to build an alliance in Zhao to oppose Chu, so he sent troops to support Chen Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Rong wished to build an alliance in Zhao to strengthen his opposition to Chu, so he sent troops to support Chen Yu.

sentences.zh: 陳餘因悉三縣兵襲常山王張耳。

translations.literal: Chen Yu then mustered all the troops from his three counties and attacked Zhang Er, the King of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu then mustered all the troops from his three counties and launched an attack on Zhang Er, the King of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 張耳敗走，念諸侯無可歸者，曰：「漢王與我有舊故，而項羽又彊，立我，我欲之楚。」

translations.literal: Zhang Er was defeated and fled. Considering that there was no lord he could go to, he said: 'The King of Han and I have an old friendship, and though Xiang Yu is powerful and established me, I wish to go to Chu.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er was routed and fled. Considering that there was no lord he could turn to, he said, 'The King of Han and I are old friends. Xiang Yu is powerful, and it was he who made me king, but I wish to go to Chu.'

sentences.zh: 甘公曰：「漢王之入關，五星聚東井。

translations.literal: Master Gan said: 'When the King of Han entered the Pass, the five planets gathered in the constellation of Dongjing.
translations.idiomatic: His adviser Master Gan said, 'When the King of Han entered the Pass, the five planets converged in the constellation of the Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 東井者，秦分也。

translations.literal: The Eastern Well is the celestial domain of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Well corresponds to the domain of Qin.

sentences.zh: 先至必霸。

translations.literal: The one who arrives first will surely become hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: The one who arrives there first is destined to rule.

sentences.zh: 楚雖彊，後必屬漢。」

translations.literal: Though Chu is strong, in the end it will surely belong to Han.'
translations.idiomatic: Though Chu is mighty now, in the end all will belong to Han.'

sentences.zh: 故耳走漢。

translations.literal: Therefore, Zhang Er fled to Han.
translations.idiomatic: And so Zhang Er fled to Han.

sentences.zh: 漢王亦還定三秦，方圍章邯廢丘。

translations.literal: The King of Han had also returned and pacified the Three Qin, and was then besieging Zhang Han at Feiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Han had by then returned and pacified the Three Qin, and was laying siege to Zhang Han at Feiqiu.

sentences.zh: 張耳謁漢王，漢王厚遇之。

translations.literal: Zhang Er went to see the King of Han, and the King of Han received him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Er presented himself before the King of Han, who received him with great generosity.

sentences.zh: 陳餘已敗張耳，皆復收趙地，迎趙王於代，復為趙王。

translations.literal: After Chen Yu had defeated Zhang Er, he recovered all the lands of Zhao, welcomed the King of Zhao from Dai, and restored him as King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Zhang Er, Chen Yu recovered all the territory of Zhao. He welcomed King Zhao Xie back from Dai and restored him to the throne of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 趙王德陳餘，立以為代王。

translations.literal: The King of Zhao was grateful to Chen Yu and made him King of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao, grateful for Chen Yu's service, made him King of Dai.

sentences.zh: 陳餘為趙王弱，國初定，不之國，留傅趙王，而使夏說以相國守代。

translations.literal: Chen Yu, because the King of Zhao was weak and the state had just been settled, did not go to his own kingdom but stayed to serve as tutor to the King of Zhao, while sending Xia Yue to govern Dai as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Zhao was weak, and the state had only recently been restored, so Chen Yu did not depart for his own kingdom. Instead, he remained to serve as the king's tutor, while sending Xia Yue to govern Dai as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 漢二年，東擊楚，使使告趙，欲與俱。

translations.literal: In the second year of Han, the King of Han marched east to attack Chu and sent envoys to inform Zhao, wishing them to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Han, the King of Han marched east against Chu and sent envoys to Zhao, inviting them to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 陳餘曰：「漢殺張耳乃從。」

translations.literal: Chen Yu said: 'We will join you only if Han kills Zhang Er.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu replied, 'We will join you only after Han puts Zhang Er to death.'

sentences.zh: 於是漢王求人類張耳者斬之，持其頭遺陳餘。

translations.literal: Thereupon the King of Han found a man who resembled Zhang Er, had him beheaded, and sent his head to Chen Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Han found a man who resembled Zhang Er, had him beheaded, and sent the head to Chen Yu.

sentences.zh: 陳餘乃遣兵助漢。

translations.literal: Chen Yu then sent troops to assist Han.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yu then dispatched troops to assist Han.

sentences.zh: 漢之敗於彭城西，陳餘亦復覺張耳不死，即背漢。

translations.literal: When Han was defeated west of Pengcheng, Chen Yu also discovered that Zhang Er was not dead, and immediately turned against Han.
translations.idiomatic: After Han's defeat west of Pengcheng, Chen Yu discovered that Zhang Er was in fact still alive, and he immediately turned against Han.

sentences.zh: 漢三年，韓信已定魏地，遣張耳與韓信擊破趙井陘，斬陳餘泜水上，追殺趙王歇襄國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Han, Han Xin had already pacified the land of Wei. Zhang Er was sent with Han Xin to attack and defeat Zhao at Jingxing. Chen Yu was beheaded on the banks of the Zhi River, and King Zhao Xie was pursued and killed at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Han, after Han Xin had pacified the territory of Wei, he and Zhang Er were sent to attack Zhao. They shattered the Zhao army at Jingxing, beheaded Chen Yu on the banks of the Zhi River, and pursued King Zhao Xie to Xiangguo, where he was killed.

sentences.zh: 漢立張耳為趙王。

translations.literal: Han established Zhang Er as King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Han then established Zhang Er as King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 漢五年，張耳薨，謚為景王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Han, Zhang Er died, and he was posthumously titled King Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Han, Zhang Er died. He was given the posthumous title King Jing.

sentences.zh: 子敖嗣立為趙王。

translations.literal: His son Ao succeeded him and was established as King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Ao succeeded him as King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 高祖長女魯元公主為趙王敖后。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Luyuan, became the queen of King Ao of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu's eldest daughter, Princess Luyuan, became Queen of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 漢七年，高祖從平城過趙，趙王朝夕袒韛蔽，自上食，禮甚卑，有子婿禮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Han, Emperor Gaozu passed through Zhao on his return from Pingcheng. The King of Zhao waited on him morning and evening, baring his arms and wearing an apron, personally serving food. His manner was extremely humble, observing the etiquette of a son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Han, Emperor Gaozu passed through Zhao on his return from Pingcheng. The King of Zhao attended him morning and evening, baring his arms and tying on an apron to serve the food himself. His deference was extreme, befitting a son-in-law rather than a king.

sentences.zh: 高祖箕踞詈，甚慢易之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sat with his legs spread wide, cursing freely, and treated him with great contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sat sprawled with his legs apart, swearing and berating him. He treated the King of Zhao with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 趙相貫高、趙午等年六十餘，故張耳客也。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of Zhao, Guan Gao, Zhao Wu, and others, all over sixty years old, were former retainers of Zhang Er.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor of Zhao, Guan Gao, along with Zhao Wu and other men over sixty years of age, had all been retainers of Zhang Er.

sentences.zh: 生平為氣，乃怒曰：「吾王孱王也！」

translations.literal: They were men of spirit by nature, and they said angrily: 'Our king is a weak king!'
translations.idiomatic: These were men of fierce pride, and they said in fury, 'Our king is a weakling!'

sentences.zh: 說王曰：「夫天下豪桀并起，能者先立。

translations.literal: They addressed the king, saying: 'Heroes throughout the realm have risen together; the capable are the first to establish themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They went to the king and said, 'Heroes have risen across the realm, and the capable are the first to stake their claim.

sentences.zh: 今王事高祖甚恭，而高祖無禮，請為王殺之！」

translations.literal: Now the King serves Emperor Gaozu with the utmost respect, yet Gaozu shows no courtesy. We beg to kill him for the King!'
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty serves Emperor Gaozu with the deepest reverence, yet the Emperor shows you nothing but contempt. Allow us to kill him for you!'

sentences.zh: 張敖齧其指出血，曰：「君何言之誤！

translations.literal: Zhang Ao bit his finger until it bled and said: 'How wrong your words are!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ao bit his finger until it bled and cried, 'What terrible things you say!

sentences.zh: 且先人亡國，賴高祖得復國，德流子孫，秋豪皆高祖力也。

translations.literal: My father lost his kingdom, and it was thanks to Emperor Gaozu that it was restored. This grace flows down to his descendants—every particle of it was through Gaozu's power.
translations.idiomatic: My father lost his kingdom, and it was Emperor Gaozu who restored it. This grace extends to his descendants—every last bit of it was Gaozu's doing.

sentences.zh: 願君無復出口。」

translations.literal: I beg you never to speak of this again.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, never speak of this again.'

sentences.zh: 貫高、趙午等十餘人皆相謂曰：「乃吾等非也。

translations.literal: Guan Gao, Zhao Wu, and more than ten others all said to one another: 'We were wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Gao, Zhao Wu, and more than ten others conferred among themselves: 'We were wrong to involve the king.

sentences.zh: 吾王長者，不倍德。

translations.literal: Our king is a man of virtue; he would not betray a kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Our king is a man of integrity. He will not betray a debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 且吾等義不辱，今怨高祖辱我王，故欲殺之，何乃汙王為乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, by our code of honor we cannot endure insult. Now we resent Gaozu for humiliating our king, so we wish to kill him—why should we drag the king into disgrace?
translations.idiomatic: Our code of honor will not suffer insult. We resent Gaozu for humiliating our king, and so we wish to kill him. Why should we drag the king into this disgrace?

sentences.zh: 令事成歸王，事敗獨身坐耳。」

translations.literal: If we succeed, the credit goes to the king; if we fail, we alone will bear the punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: If we succeed, the credit goes to the king. If we fail, we alone will bear the consequences.'

sentences.zh: 漢八年，上從東垣還，過趙，貫高等乃壁人柏人，要之置廁。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Han, when the Emperor was returning from Dongyuan and passing through Zhao, Guan Gao and the others concealed men in the walls at Bairen, planning to waylay him at the privy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Han, as the Emperor was returning from Dongyuan and passing through Zhao, Guan Gao and his conspirators hid assassins in the walls at Bairen, intending to waylay him at the privy.

sentences.zh: 上過欲宿，心動，問曰：「縣名為何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor was passing through and was about to stay the night when his heart stirred. He asked: 'What is the name of this county?'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was about to spend the night there when he felt a sudden unease. He asked, 'What is the name of this county?'

sentences.zh: 曰：「柏人。」

translations.literal: They replied: 'Bairen.'
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: 'Bairen.'

sentences.zh: 「柏人者，迫於人也！」

translations.literal: 'Bairen—"pressed by men"!'
translations.idiomatic: 'Bairen!' he exclaimed. 'That sounds like "pressed by men"!'

sentences.zh: 不宿而去。

translations.literal: He did not stay the night and left.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to spend the night and departed at once.

sentences.zh: 漢九年，貫高怨家知其謀，乃上變告之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Han, enemies of Guan Gao learned of his plot and reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Han, enemies of Guan Gao learned of the plot and reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是上皆并逮捕趙王、貫高等。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor had the King of Zhao, Guan Gao, and the others all arrested together.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the arrest of the King of Zhao along with Guan Gao and all the other conspirators.

sentences.zh: 十餘人皆爭自剄，貫高獨怒罵曰：「誰令公為之？

translations.literal: More than ten of the conspirators all vied to cut their own throats, but Guan Gao alone cursed angrily, saying: 'Who told you to do this?
translations.idiomatic: More than ten of the conspirators tried to slit their own throats, but Guan Gao alone raged at them: 'Who told you to do this?

sentences.zh: 今王實無謀，而并捕王；

translations.literal: The king truly had no part in the plot, yet the king has been arrested too;
translations.idiomatic: The king truly had no part in our plot, yet they have arrested him too.

sentences.zh: 公等皆死，誰白王不反者！」

translations.literal: If you all die, who will clear the king of the charge of rebellion!'
translations.idiomatic: If all of you die now, who will be left to prove that the king is innocent?'

sentences.zh: 乃轞車膠致，與王詣長安。

translations.literal: They were then placed in sealed prison carts and taken together with the king to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: They were loaded into sealed prison carts and transported to Chang'an along with the king.

sentences.zh: 治張敖之罪。

translations.literal: Zhang Ao's crimes were investigated.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation was opened into Zhang Ao's crimes.

sentences.zh: 上乃詔趙群臣賓客有敢從王皆族。

translations.literal: The Emperor then decreed that any minister or guest of Zhao who dared to follow the king would have their entire clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then issued an edict declaring that any minister or retainer of Zhao who dared follow the king would have their entire clan put to death.

sentences.zh: 貫高與客孟舒等十餘人，皆自髡鉗，為王家奴，從來。

translations.literal: Guan Gao and guests such as Meng Shu, more than ten men in all, all shaved their heads and placed iron collars around their necks, becoming household slaves of the king, and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Gao, along with Meng Shu and more than ten other retainers, shaved their heads and clamped iron collars around their necks, disguising themselves as the king's household slaves in order to follow him.

sentences.zh: 貫高至，對獄，曰：「獨吾屬為之，王實不知。」

translations.literal: When Guan Gao arrived and faced trial, he said: 'Only we did this; the king truly did not know.'
translations.idiomatic: When Guan Gao was brought to trial, he declared, 'We alone are responsible. The king truly knew nothing of it.'

sentences.zh: 吏治榜笞數千，刺剟，身無可擊者，終不復言。

translations.literal: The officials beat him with clubs and bamboo thousands of times and stabbed him with needles until there was no spot left on his body to strike, but he never changed his statement.
translations.idiomatic: The officials flogged him thousands of times and pricked his flesh with needles until there was not a spot left on his body to strike, but he never changed his testimony.

sentences.zh: 呂后數言張王以魯元公主故，不宜有此。

translations.literal: Empress Lu repeatedly said that King Zhang, because of Princess Luyuan, should not be treated this way.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lu repeatedly argued that Zhang Ao, as the husband of Princess Luyuan, should not be treated this way.

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「使張敖據天下，豈少而女乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said angrily: 'If Zhang Ao held the whole realm, would he lack for your daughter!'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said in a fury, 'If Zhang Ao held the whole realm, do you think he would lack for women? Your daughter would mean nothing to him!'

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to relent.

sentences.zh: 廷尉以貫高事辭聞，上曰：「壯士！

translations.literal: When the Commandant of Justice reported the details of Guan Gao's testimony, the Emperor said: 'A brave man!
translations.idiomatic: When the Commandant of Justice presented the details of Guan Gao's testimony, the Emperor exclaimed, 'A brave man indeed!

sentences.zh: 誰知者，以私問之。」

translations.literal: Who knows him? Have someone question him privately.'
translations.idiomatic: Does anyone know him? Have someone question him in private.'

sentences.zh: 中大夫泄公曰：「臣之邑子，素知之。

translations.literal: The Palace Grandee Xie Gong said: 'He is a fellow townsman of mine; I have always known him.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Grandee Xie Gong said, 'He is from my hometown. I have known him all my life.

sentences.zh: 此固趙國立名義不侵為然諾者也。」

translations.literal: He is one of those men from Zhao who are famous for upholding honor and keeping their word without fail.'
translations.idiomatic: He is one of those men of Zhao renowned for their honor and for keeping their word at any cost.'

sentences.zh: 上使泄公持節問之箯輿前。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Xie Gong, bearing the imperial staff, to question him before the prisoner's litter.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Xie Gong, bearing the imperial staff of authority, to question Guan Gao before his prison litter.

sentences.zh: 仰視曰：「泄公邪？」

translations.literal: Guan Gao looked up and said: 'Is that Xie Gong?'
translations.idiomatic: Guan Gao looked up and said, 'Is that Xie Gong?'

sentences.zh: 泄公勞苦如生平驩，與語，問張王果有計謀不。

translations.literal: Xie Gong comforted him as if they were old friends, spoke with him, and asked whether King Zhang had truly been involved in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Gong consoled him warmly, speaking as though they were old friends, and asked whether King Zhang had truly been involved in the plot.

sentences.zh: 高曰：「人情寧不各愛其父母妻子乎？

translations.literal: Gao said: 'Is it not human nature for everyone to love their parents, wife, and children?
translations.idiomatic: Guan Gao said, 'Is it not human nature to love one's own parents, wife, and children?

sentences.zh: 今吾三族皆以論死，豈以王易吾親哉！

translations.literal: Now my three clans have all been condemned to death—would I trade my own family for the king!
translations.idiomatic: All three branches of my clan have been condemned to death. Do you think I would sacrifice my own family to shield the king?

sentences.zh: 顧為王實不反，獨吾等為之。」

translations.literal: But the truth is that the king did not rebel; only we did it.'
translations.idiomatic: But the truth is that the king did not rebel. We alone are responsible.'

sentences.zh: 具道本指所以為者王不知狀。

translations.literal: He then explained in full the original plan and how the king had no knowledge of it.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave a full account of the original plot and the circumstances proving that the king had known nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 於是泄公入，具以報，上乃赦趙王。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xie Gong entered the palace, reported everything in full, and the Emperor pardoned the King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Gong returned to the palace and reported everything. The Emperor thereupon pardoned the King of Zhao.
